title: Two Poitou intelligence notes of 1586 in Matignon's Cipher-3: BnF fr. 15572 f. 276 and fr. 15571 f. 179 (catalogue item 12)

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 15572 f. 276 (Gallica btv1b9061879d, canvas 285 right)
documents.route: unknown informant, Poitou -> the Matignon / royal side

plaintext.source: No decipherment of the leaf; Tomokiyo publishes its opening line (cryptiana), which the reading matches.

transcription.source: alejandrozarco (PR #25): two independent sign-by-sign readings (read1.txt, read2.txt) from deskewed line crops of the Gallica image, reconciled on the image (read_final.txt); count from f276/scripts/measure.py
transcription.notes: 22 cipher lines; the two reads agree on 693 of 739 signs (93.8%).

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 15571 f. 179 (Gallica btv1b90618802, canvas 187 left, bound upside down)
documents.route: unknown writer -> the Matignon / royal side

plaintext.source: Satoshi Tomokiyo's interlinear decipherment in magenta on his image of the leaf (cryptiana BnFfr15571f179.jpg, 680 px), never published as text

transcription.source: alejandrozarco (PR #25): two independent sign-by-sign readings (readA.txt, readB.txt) without Tomokiyo's image, reconciled against the image and his magenta (read_final.txt); count from f276/scripts/measure.py
transcription.notes: 21 cipher lines; the two reads agree on 472 of 516 signs (91.5%).

system.summary: Matignon's Cipher-3 (Tomokiyo's partial table): a homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with word signs (60 faire, a beta-like sign de, 20 la, 18 le, p-with-stroke pour, C with n que, ∴ qui, ### et) and a null (plain v).
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's partial Cipher-3 table (cryptiana, Henry III's Cipher with Ambassadors), checked on the deciphered sibling ff. 277r-278r / 279r-280r
system.notes: Split on 14 Oct 2026 from matignon1586 under the one-key rule: that entry joined these two Cipher-3 leaves with the Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1 despatches. The two leaves share names (Iehan Durant, La Rousière) and belong together; deciphered siblings in the same key: f. 189 (in f. 190), ff. 277-278 (in ff. 279-280), f. 282 (margin).

prior_solution.where: f. 276: no reading beyond Tomokiyo's published opening; fr. 15571 f. 179: Tomokiyo's interlinear decipherment on his image (cryptiana), unpublished as text

conditions.human_role: Contributed: alejandrozarco did the transcription, alignment and reading (PR #25, 6-7 Oct 2026); the project reviewed and re-measured it.
tools: f276/scripts/align_em.py (hard-EM alignment of a blind transcription of f. 277r against ff. 279-280)

solution.what: Located the two Cipher-3 leaves on the images: fr. 15571 f. 179 at canvas 187 left (bound upside down; first listed as 'f. 178v, fourth hand') and fr. 15572 f. 276 at canvas 285 right; siblings ff. 277r-278r deciphered in ff. 279-280.

alejandrozarco (PR #25): Tomokiyo's partial Cipher-3 table checked by hard-EM alignment of a blind transcription of sibling f. 277r against its contemporary decipherment on ff. 279-280; values added (### = et, two-stroke # = i, dotted v = u, S-shape = q and others).
alejandrozarco (PR #25): f. 276 (22 lines) and fr. 15571 f. 179 (21 lines) transcribed sign by sign twice, independently; reads agree on 93.8% (f. 276) and 91.5% (f. 179) of signs.

alejandrozarco (PR #25): f. 276 deciphered with the Cipher-3 key, 698/734 signs (95.1%) in lexical runs (fr-henri4 word list); f. 179 transcribed and checked against Tomokiyo's unpublished magenta interlinear decipherment, 466/509 (91.6%). Poitou faction report naming La Rousiere, la Mare, Iehan Durant, Lansac.

Review of PR #25: measure.py re-run reproduces 698/734 and 466/509; 50 shuffled keys give median 6.3% / 3.1% (max 21.5% / 21.0%); line structure of f. 276 L01, L21, L22 and f. 179 L18 (blot), L21 checked on the Gallica natives.

alejandrozarco, after the PR #25 review: measure.py and control_shuffle.py now take their lexicon from the shared lang/ model fr-1600-letters (corpora.text + lm.norm 'early', words >= 20 occurrences) instead of bundled word lists, which are removed. f. 276 706/734 (96.2%; 50 shuffled keys median 6.9%), f. 179 473/509 (92.9%; median 3.5%); the difference from the word list is mainly 'veullent' reaching 20 occurrences under lang normalisation. f. 276 L18 read as 'redoute la [K]; quelque chose', making the C-with-epsilon sign q and K a one-sign code word (paix? Ligue? Royne?).

Split from the former combined target matignon1586 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): the two Cipher-3 leaves are their own entry; f276/ and f179/ moved here. measure.py re-run on both read_final.txt files reproduces 706/734 and 473/509.

outcome.method_basis: f. 276 was deciphered with Tomokiyo's partial Cipher-3 table, checked and extended on the deciphered sibling ff. 277r/279-280; f. 179 was transcribed blind and reconciled with Tomokiyo's interlinear decipherment.

parts.label: f. 276
parts.basis: Tomokiyo's Cipher-3 table, checked on ff. 277r/279-280 and extended (### = et and other values); 706 of 734 signs (96.2%) in sense runs, measured; 50 shuffled keys median 6.9%

parts.label: fr. 15571 f. 179
parts.basis: Tomokiyo's interlinear decipherment in magenta on his image of the leaf, checked by two blind sign-by-sign readings with his key; 473 of 509 signs (92.9%), measured; shuffled median 3.5%

outcome.fraction_read_source: f276/scripts/measure.py over f276/read_final.txt (706/734) and f179/read_final.txt (473/509): 1179 of 1243 signs inside sense runs (lang model fr-1600-letters, the targets/matignon1586/measure.py rule); re-run 14 Oct 2026

gaps.item: f. 276 L18 'K' and L14 'C with o inside', one-sign code words not in Tomokiyo's table
gaps.detail: Each occurs once (paix? Ligue? Royne? for K); neither recurs on these two leaves; the deciphered Cipher-3 siblings f. 189/190, f. 282 and fr. 15570 ff. 271-273 have not been searched for them.

gaps.item: f. 179 L13, the omega-with-overbar code sign (a person, Navarre?)
gaps.detail: One occurrence; Tomokiyo's magenta at 680 px does not settle it.

gaps.item: blots: f. 276 L04 after 'de lui', f. 179 L18 after 'en'
gaps.detail: Ink blots on the leaf; checked on the Gallica natives.

gaps.item: f. 276 L22 closing (one or two signs before the plaintext 'ou...'), f. 179 L20 'de la D[...]use' and a struck sign, and a few short spans
gaps.detail: Faint or struck signs at the edge of the slip; the rest of the 28 + 36 unread signs are words the period lexicon holds fewer than 20 times (prieure, escriuent).

outcome.notes: Contributed by alejandrozarco (PR #25, 6-7 Oct 2026), reviewed and re-measured here. Content: a Poitou intelligence note on the Catholic factions round La Roussière (f. 276) and a sibling naming Pons, sickness in the army and Lansac for the sea army (f. 179).
